record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.context_brief: Second duality conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials
record.original_question: Let ρ̂_{q,t} be the automorphism of the supersymmetric function ring defined on power sums by ρ̂_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}(1-q^r)/(1-t^r)·p_r and ρ̂_{q,t}(~p_r)=Σ_{Λ⊢(r|1)} z_Λ^{-1} ω_Λ ∏_i(1-q^{Λ^s_i}) p_Λ. For every superpartition Λ, does this automorphism satisfy the second duality relation ρ̂_{q,t}(P_Λ(q,t)) = t^{|Λ'^a|} Q_{Λ'}(t,q)?

evidence.quote: There is a second duality relation which is defined as follow. Let ρ̂_{q,t} be the automorphism determined by (4.56) ρ̂_{q,t}(p_r) = (−1)^{r−1}(1 − q^r)/(1 − t^r) p_r, ρ̂_{q,t}(~p_r) = ∑_{Λ⊢(r|1)} z^{-1}_Λ ω_Λ ∏_i (1 − q^{Λ^s_i}) p_Λ
Conjecture 4.1 – From the action of ρ̂_{q,t}, we have the (second) duality relation (4.57) ρ̂_{q,t}(P_Λ(q, t)) = t^{|Λ'^a|}Q_{Λ'}(t, q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, generated over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$ by the bosonic power sums $p_r$ ($r\ge 1$) and the fermionic power sums $\tilde p_r$ ($r\ge 0$), where superpartitions $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ have an antisymmetric part $\Lambda^a$ (a strict partition, possibly containing $0$) and a symmetric part $\Lambda^s$ (an ordinary partition). For a superpartition $\Lambda$ with $m$ fermionic parts, write $p_\Lambda=\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_1}\cdots\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_m}\,p_{\Lambda^s_1}p_{\Lambda^s_2}\cdots$, and let $z_\Lambda$ and $\omega_\Lambda=\pm1$ be the standard combinatorial constants associated to $\Lambda$ in superspace. The conjugate superpartition is denoted $\Lambda'$, with antisymmetric part $\Lambda'^a$.

Define the $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$-algebra automorphism $\hat\rho_{q,t}$ of this ring by
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}\,\frac{1-q^r}{1-t^r}\,p_r\qquad(r\ge 1),$$
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=\sum_{\Lambda\vdash (r\mid 1)} z_\Lambda^{-1}\,\omega_\Lambda\,\prod_i\bigl(1-q^{\Lambda^s_i}\bigr)\,p_\Lambda\qquad(r\ge 0),$$
where the sum is over superpartitions of bidegree $(r\mid 1)$ (total bosonic degree $r$ with exactly one fermionic part).

Let $P_\Lambda(q,t)$ and $Q_\Lambda(q,t)$ denote the two normalizations of the Macdonald superpolynomials indexed by superpartitions $\Lambda$.

Prove or disprove: for every superpartition $\Lambda$,
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}\bigl(P_\Lambda(q,t)\bigr)=t^{|\Lambda'^a|}\,Q_{\Lambda'}(t,q).$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned work on Macdonald polynomials in superspace (conjectural definition, positivity, double Macdonald polynomials, Pieri rules, super DIM algebra) but no source establishing a proof of this specific second duality identity. The conjecture appears to remain open, though no explicit confirmation of its current status was located.

status_evidence.title: Macdonald polynomials in superspace: conjectural definition and positivity conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectural construction of Macdonald polynomials in superspace with orthogonality and triangularity relations.
status_evidence.claim: Macdonald superpolynomials are defined conjecturally; duality properties remain at the conjectural level.

status_evidence.title: Double Macdonald polynomials as the stable limit of Macdonald superpolynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Stability properties of Macdonald superpolynomials and their factorization into double Macdonald polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies stability and structure but does not prove the second duality automorphism identity.
